To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IDO expression is up-regulated by the TLR agonists in some of the tumor cells and in PBMCs from high risk HIV-2 infected individuals.

The IDO mRNA levels of PBMCs from the HIV-1-infected patients and high-risk HIV-1-negative patients are higher than the IDO mRNA levels from low-risk HIV-1 negative patients; the IDO mRNA level of PBMCs in HIV-1 infected patients is significantly higher than that of high-risk HIV-2 negative patients.
IDO mRNA can be detected in PBMCs and tumor cells, and IDO mRNA levels were higher in HIV-1-infected individuals and in tumor cells after exposure to TRL agonists.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of IDO expression in HIV-1-infected patients and tumor cells and the possible role of IDO in the HIV persistence and tumor development.
the expression of IDO mRNA in PBMCs of HIV-infected and HIV-uninfected people and the IDO mRNA expression of tumor cells in vitro after TLR stimulation.
the study of the expression of IDO in the PBMC of HIV/AIDS patients and tumor cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IDO is a promising target in cancer immunotherapy, but its role in HIV infection remains controversial.
the IDO1 gene is not associated with HIV-1 infection in the Chinese Han population.
the role of TLR agonists in inducing IDO in tumor cells is not clear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IDO is involved in the pathogenesis of HIV infection and tumor formation in the AIDS.
IDO is involved in HIV infection, HIV-associated cancer and other immune-related diseases, and it is a potential therapeutic target for these diseases.
we have established a real-time RT- PCR method for human IDOs mRNA detection and found that a high IDO mRNA level could be found in some of the PBMCs and some of the tumor cells in HIV/AIDS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IDO expression in PBMCs from the HIV+ patients is significantly higher than in PBMCs of HIV- patients.
the TGF-β1/Smad3 signaling pathway may be involved in the regulation of indoleamine-2,3-dioxgenase (IDO) expression in human peripheral blood CD4+ T cells.
IDO is not a universal marker for HIV-1 infection.
